A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAPS++ work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material. Content can be reliably matched across pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original FFHQ and ImageNet reconstruction experiments, efficiency and robustness analyses, and supplementary phase-retrieval and hyperparameter results.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds the FFHQ inpainting ablation in Table 4.

M1.justification: The proposed initialization-refinement procedure, Tweedie/RK4 switching, likelihood-only updates, re-noising, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The added experimental variants test the existing method's design.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same FFHQ and ImageNet restoration tasks, including supplementary phase retrieval. Table 4 uses the already evaluated FFHQ inpainting task without introducing a distinct dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds comparisons against DAPS-100 without prior-gradient refinement, DAPS with Tweedie initialization, and DAPS with Tweedie/RK4 initialization. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new inpainting ablation compares initialization and refinement combinations under a stated common budget of 100 diffusion NFEs. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, preprocessing, and noise settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 4 add a focused ablation testing prior-gradient removal and initialization choices on FFHQ inpainting. Earlier gradient diagnostics, noise robustness tests, initialization examples, and supplementary sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure S2 retains the same phase-retrieval mean and standard-deviation reporting. Table 4 adds point estimates without new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds results including SSIM/LPIPS of 0.741/0.186 for DAPS with Tweedie initialization and 0.712/0.192 for DAPS with Tweedie/RK4, plus inpainting runtimes. Its DAPS++ score of 0.812/0.141 already appears in v3 Table 1. Existing Tables 1–3 and supplementary results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, method equations, Lipschitz assumptions and proof, and warm-start convergence derivations are retained. Supplementary Sections S1.1–S1.3 contain no theoretical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that diffusion primarily supplies initialization and that decoupling improves reconstruction efficiency. The added ablation supplies support without changing these claims' scope.

C2.justification: The new Section 4.3 discussion qualifies direct Tweedie initialization as producing overly smooth inpainting reconstructions with insufficient detail, connecting this limitation to the existing thresholded RK4 transition. Earlier interpretations and phase-retrieval limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 4 explicitly documents the initialization and refinement configurations of the new controls, including two-step Euler, Tweedie, Tweedie/RK4, and the presence or absence of prior-gradient refinement. Existing pseudocode, hardware descriptions, and supplementary hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 expands the discussion of diffusion models as plug-and-play denoising priors and adds Wu et al., Principled Probabilistic Imaging Using Diffusion Models as Plug-and-Play Priors. Other referenced works are retained, with citation renumbering.

P1.justification: v4 adds limited explanatory prose in Sections 2.2 and 4.3, adjusts cross-references and wording, and consolidates author affiliations. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 4, enlarges Figure 4, and relocates existing displays, including Table 2 and Figure 5. Existing figure content and supplementary displays are retained; the changes are localized rather than a document-wide redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 4 modestly strengthens validation by comparing prior-gradient removal and initialization choices at a common diffusion-NFE budget. The expanded plug-and-play discussion also improves research context. These gains are limited to a focused experiment and clarification; the method, theory, main benchmark results, and supplementary evidence remain unchanged.
